newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says wishes U.S. had held off on Iraq attack.
newsitem.headline: Spain says wishes U.S. had held off on Iraq attack.

text.p: Spain, one of the United States' NATO allies, said on Tuesday it wished Washington had delayed its strike against Iraqi targets.
"(Our reaction) is one of understanding, although we would have wanted that armed intervention to be, at least, postponed," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told a radio interviewer.

Matutes did not elaborate. His interviewer had asked him whether Madrid's reaction was one of "understanding and support". The Pentagon said the attacks were launched in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds.
Washington told its allies of its attack plans late on Monday after consulting Saudi Arabia, British Prime Minister John Major and French President Jacques Chirac, Matutes told Ser radio.
Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar was going ahead with a scheduled trip to Latin America as there was no reason to change plans, the foreign minister added.
Spain said the U.S. attack against Iraqi positions was aimed at a missile base.
